_spec.purpose: Demand model for Cook Inlet Gas Watch. The coefficients live here as data rather than as constants inside scripts/gaswatch_collect.py, so a refit is a data change with its own commit and never a code change. Every collected record carries a copy of this block, so a record always states the model that produced its numbers.
_spec.refit_procedure: Bump version, edit the coefficients, update every backtest expect_* value to what the new coefficients produce, append a model_history entry naming the reason and the data behind it. Then run python3 scripts/gaswatch_collect.py --self-test, which recomputes every backtest and fails if this file is internally inconsistent.
_spec.honesty_note: This model is calibrated to two published figures. It is not fit to observed sendout, because observed sendout is not public. Nothing derived from it may be published as a safety verdict, a shortfall prediction, or an all clear.

calibration: average day 190 MMcf/d, design day 390 MMcf/d at HDD 75
fit_source: published figures, not fit to observed sendout

mass_balance.identity: D = P + W, therefore P = D - W
mass_balance.note: D is modeled demand, W is the measured CINGSA inventory draw. What falls out of P is field production plus any Hilcorp storage draw combined, which is why the field is named non_cingsa_supply_mmcfd and is never called production.

backtests.description: The coldest day in the twelve year PANC record, 2026-01-08, at HDD 76
The 2025 to 2026 season integrated over a full year at 10,545 heating degree days
backtests.note: A 365 day base term gives 71.7 Bcf and a 364 day base term gives 71.6. The 0.1 Bcf gap is the day count, not the coefficients. Stated regional consumption is near 75 Bcf, so the model runs about 4 percent light across a season and that gap is published, not hidden.

model_history.reason: First hypothesis. Two point calibration against the published average day and design day figures, standing in until enough observed sendout exists to fit against.
